sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
Carve — Dealing physical damage to champions reduces the target's Armor by 6% for 6 seconds. (stacks 5 times).
debuffs do not stack with themselves unless stated, and are always temporary or conditional (they do not persist after the target's death)

Whether an effect applied several times to the same unit stacks or not: different effects always stack with each other; a non-stacking effect only resets its duration on reapplication; auras do not stack with themselves (a unit affected by two identical auras receives the effect once)

step_1_is_the_magnitude_legal.wiki_rule: 6% armor reduction per Carve stack, max 5 stacks, hard cap 30% on the target
step_1_is_the_magnitude_legal.conclusion: 0.24 is exactly the sanctioned value for ONE Carve instance (≤ 0.30 cap). The old leaf's magnitude was never the defect; its existence as an additional instance is.

step_2_what_factor_1_15_implies.identity: amplification of a fractional armor reduction f on running armor R = m(R·(1−f)) / m(R) = (100 + R) / (100 + R·(1−f))
step_2_what_factor_1_15_implies.conclusion: The removed entry was applied to a still-POSITIVE running armor of ~119, i.e. it was a further shred on top of already-shredded armor — not a no-op, and not the docs' 'percentage reduction cannot act below 0 armor' guard case (that guard would yield factor 1.0, and on negative armor a shrink of |R| gives factor < 1, never 1.15). So the entry was materially inflating damage.

step_3_cap_violation_of_multiple_instanc.conclusion: Any n ≥ 2 exceeds the 30% Carve maximum stated by both the Wiki branch text and Riot's own description. Carve is a debuff ON THE TARGET (both texts are phrased target-side: 'applies a stack ... to an enemy champion', 'reduces the target's Armor by 6% ... (stacks 5 times)'), so a roster in which several allies each carry a Black Cleaver still yields exactly one Carve debuff, capped at 5 stacks / 30%. Per-holder duplication is not a game behavior.

step_4_structural_read_of_the_leaf.observation: The leaf is index [3] of a per-event list and its new state is <absent> — i.e. the list at event 46 got shorter, not re-valued. This is the shape of a de-duplication, not of a magnitude correction.
step_4_structural_read_of_the_leaf.supporting_scan: Across the whole cached item cache, Black Cleaver 3071 is the ONLY source of percent armor reduction (the one other reduction item, 447112 Flesheater 'Hack the Meat', is FLAT: 'reduces the target's armor and magic resistance by 3 ... total resistances reduction of 30'). A support-side list of type armor_reduction_percent with ≥ 4 entries therefore cannot be four distinct item sources; the entries are per-holder repeats of the same Carve debuff.
step_4_structural_read_of_the_leaf.scenario_name: 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' names exactly the two shared, target-side team debuffs (Carve armor reduction; Bloodsong's Expose Weakness 'increased damage from all sources'), i.e. it is the fixture for testing that team-shared debuffs are counted once per target rather than once per holder.

independent_computation.correct_value: <absent> — event 46's support_resistance_reduction list must carry at most ONE 'Black Cleaver — Carve' entry (fraction ≤ 0.30, 0.24 under the documented 0.8·max_stacks model). The instance at index [3] is a duplicate of a debuff the target can only hold once, and removing it is required to keep total Carve reduction within the wiki-stated 30% maximum.

confidence_and_caveats: The sibling entries of the list could not be inspected: the golden baseline lives under scripts/, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this investigator from reading. The verdict rests on (a) BC being the only percent-armor-reduction source in the cached item data, (b) Carve being a target-side debuff capped at 5 stacks / 30% in both Wiki and Riot text, (c) debuffs not stacking with themselves, and (d) the change being a list shortening rather than a re-valuation.

The verdict would flip to old_value_correct only if index [3] had been the sole Carve instance in that event's list — which would leave a scenario named for the Black Cleaver with no Carve reduction at all, and is inconsistent with a deletion at index [3] of a ≥ 4-element single-source list.

The retained fraction 0.24 is itself a documented approximation (docs/math-foundations.md § 2.3: the 0.8·max_stacks constant vs the exact Cesaro mean C − C(C−1)/(2h)); that is a separate, already-logged tuning item and does not bear on this leaf.
